CANONICAL_NAME.value: libfec -- Phil Karn's forward-error-correction library (Viterbi + Reed-Solomon)

VERSION.value: github.com/ka9q/libfec master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)

value.lineage: libfec (1995-, Phil Karn KA9Q): optimised VITERBI decoders for convolutional codes (the trellis / add-compare-select / traceback machinery) plus Reed-Solomon; the amateur-radio and deep-space FEC reference

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: maximum-likelihood decoding of noisy coded signals (hidden-state estimation)

value.built_to: recover the most-likely transmitted bit sequence from a noisy convolutionally-coded signal by the Viterbi algorithm (dynamic programming over a trellis of hidden encoder states), and to correct Reed-Solomon block errors
value.pressure: channel noise on band-limited links (satellite, deep space, radio); the decoder must find the maximum-likelihood path through an exponential state space in linear time
value.success_means: decoded bit-error rate at or below the code's theoretical curve for a given SNR; the self-tests pass

ANCESTRY.value: libfec (1995-, Phil Karn KA9Q): optimised VITERBI decoders for convolutional codes (the trellis / add-compare-select / traceback machinery) plus Reed-Solomon; the amateur-radio and deep-space FEC reference

environment.obstruction_2026-09-12: libfec's Viterbi decoders ship hand-written 32-bit x86 MMX/SSE assembly (mmxbfly27.s: `push` with 32-bit suffixes) that will not assemble on x86-64, and its 1990s configure emits an invalid -march=x86_64. The portable C path (viterbi27_port.c) exists but the lib target forces the SIMD objects. A faithful run needs an i386 world (gcc -m32 / a 32-bit container) = RUNNABLE_HISTORICAL_TOOLCHAIN, queued. Source is pinned+hashed; nothing modernised. This is a preserved 'needs an old machine' fossil, not a failure.
